final_rationale: The verdict does not improve. The Actor's response is a narrower and more careful interpretation of the same evidence, but it does not add new admissible evidence. That matters here because the key issue is not whether caveated certification sounds reasonable; it is whether the record shows the policy predicates are actually satisfied. On the available record, they are not. The supplied policy text states that rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance justifies the exposure. The Actor concedes the opposite facts remain true: the affected retirement-plan-servicing use case is still in scope, the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and unapproved, and there is no evidence that the proposed disclosure is already completed and binding before launch. That makes the Actor's narrowed position an argument for a possible future compliant state, not evidence of current compliance. Because the caveat is itself unresolved, compliant_with_caveats is not supported on this record. The claim remains inadequately supported and policy-sensitive, so the final assessment stays suspicious rather than softening based on reframing alone.
remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor reframed the same record.
The policy text provided says mitigation for a material model-card weakness requires either excluding the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance for continued exposure.
The affected retirement-plan-servicing use case remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved on this record, and does not cover the exposed retirement-servicing weakness.
There is still no admissible evidence that the proposed model-card disclosure has been completed, reviewed, or made a binding pre-launch condition.
Because the caveat itself is an unresolved compliance predicate, this does not rise to compliant_with_caveats on the present record.
Evidence access is limited to actor summary only rather than underlying documents or approvals.
